samples.summary: New slides band silently rewrites a non-number `listLevel` to 0, destroying list nesting the same PR documents as a live stored shape
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` does `block.listLevel = normalizeListLevel(asFiniteNumber(block.listLevel))`. `asFiniteNumber` returns `undefined` for anything that is not `typeof 'number'`, and `normalizeListLevel(undefined)` returns 0 — so a PUT carrying `listLevel: "2"` (a string) is rewritten to `0`, stored as 0, and echoed back as 0. The guard is a `!== undefined && !== null` presence check, so the branch is *entered* for a string and then flattens it, rather than leaving it alone. This directly contradicts the comment this same PR adds at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:95 ("`{\"type\": \"list-item\", \"listLevel\": \"2\"}` is stored as the *string* it was sent as and arrives here with that type"), whose `Number(...)` coercion is justified as load-bearing for exactly the value the new band now destroys before it is ever stored. The same flattening happens on the collaborative path in `bandBlockNumerics` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:311), and because `withTextElement` / `withShapeText` band on the way *in* and write the result back, an ordinary edit persists the 0 permanently.

samples.summary: `normalizeSlideInlines` deletes a non-numeric `fontSize` on PUT rather than leaving it, dropping stored caller content
samples.evidence: `const fontSize = normalizeFontSize(asFiniteNumber(style.fontSize)); if (fontSize === undefined) delete style.fontSize;` — `asFiniteNumber` rejects any non-`number`, so a stored/transmitted `fontSize: "12"` is deleted outright and the run silently falls back to the block default. Previously the value was preserved. Same class as the `listLevel` flattening above; it is a write-side destruction of data on a GET→edit→PUT round-trip of any deck that already holds a stringified size.

samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` returns `[]` for an empty `cols` attribute where the replaced parser returned `[0]`, collapsing a table to zero columns
samples.evidence: Old code in both readers was `(attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter(n => !isNaN(n))`, and `Number('') === 0`, so an absent/empty `cols` yielded `[0]` — one degenerate zero-width column. The new `if (!attr) return [];` yields `[]`. `computeTableLayout` sets `numCols = columnWidths.length` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153), so with `[]` the `for (c = 0; c < numCols; c++)` cell loop never runs: no `LayoutTableCell`s are built, no cell blocks are registered in `blockParentMap` (step 7 is also bounded by `numCols`), every row falls to `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT`, and the cell content becomes invisible and un-hit-testable rather than merely narrow. Reachable for any stored table whose `cols` attribute is empty (`serializeTableAttrs` writes `cols: cols.join(',')`, which is `''` for an empty `columnWidths`).

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` also truncates a legitimately tall row: the 200th fragment absorbs all remaining height onto one page
samples.evidence: `if (++fragments >= MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN) fragHeight = remaining;` is unconditional on *why* the row is tall. A row whose height is genuine content (the bands now cap the inputs, so ~200+ pages of real cell content is possible via many lines) has its 200th fragment set to the entire remainder, so pages 200..N of that row are all painted into a single overflowing fragment instead of being paginated. The bound is correct as a termination guard but is not distinguishing a poisoned height from a real one.

samples.summary: Backend slides band is narrower than the reader band it claims to mirror: inline `image` sizes are not banded on write, so PUT echoes a value every reader drops
samples.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `normalizeSlideInlines` band `lineHeight`, `listLevel`, `fontSize`, `rowHeights`, `columnWidths`, `padding` and the spans, but never call `isPaintableImageSize` on `inline.style.image`. The docs-side twin `bandBlockNumerics` does (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:323-332) and deletes the image. So a PUT with `image: {src, width: 1e9, height: 10}` is accepted, stored, and echoed back as present, while `YorkieSlidesStore.read()` / `YorkieBoardStore.read()` delete it for every viewer — breaking the stated "what the caller sees is what is stored" invariant for that one field.
searchedFor: read normalizeSlideInlines and bandSlideBlockNumerics in docs-content.controller.ts

samples.summary: Step 5d repairs `rowHeights` but leaves the derived `LayoutTableCell.height` and the cell line heights non-finite
samples.evidence: The new loop clamps only `rowHeights[r]`. `cells[r][c].height` is computed at line 196 from the same non-finite line heights and is left as `NaN`/`Infinity` on the published `LayoutTable`, as are the individual `LayoutLine.height` values the renderers and `findRowSplitHeight` read. The comment claims this is "the one place a row height becomes geometry", which holds for `rowHeights`/`rowYOffsets`/`totalHeight` but not for the per-cell geometry the same object exposes; a consumer reading `cell.height` or a line height still gets a value the clamp was meant to eliminate.
searchedFor: grep cell\.height and lc\.height under packages/docs/src/view

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. docs-content.controller.ts:1035-1037 enters the branch on any present listLevel (including a string) and assigns normalizeListLevel(asFiniteNumber(...)); asFiniteNumber (:1002-1004) returns undefined for non-numbers and normalizeListLevel (list-level.ts:43-47, `raw ?? 0`) maps that to 0, so `listLevel: "2"` is rewritten to 0, persisted by writeSlidesRoot and echoed back. No earlier guard rejects a non-number listLevel: assertValidSlideBlocks (:1084-1139) checks only style/inlines/table cells, and grep for `listLevel` under packages/backend/src/api/v1 finds only these lines. The repo itself documents the string shape as live and the coercion as load-bearing (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:88-103), and both docs read boundaries coerce with Number(...) (docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:281-282, frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:533), confirming string levels really occur. The collaborative path matches too: numeric-attrs.ts:310-312 has the same strict-typeof flatten, and yorkie-slides-store.ts:2260-2275 / 2307-2338 / 2350-2356 band on the way in and unconditionally write the banded blocks back to the CRDT, making the 0 permanent. Real, reachable, unguarded silent data rewrite — in the correctness lane.
